title: How the racial-equity section of a State Homekey application is scored
question: How are points awarded in the racial-equity part of the application these files describe, and does the scoring bear on who gets money?
finding: These three files are the State housing department's Homekey program (for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, as the files describe it). The racial-equity analysis and action plan is worth up to 10 points: 4 for a completed outcomes workbook (also a threshold to apply), up to 3 for the analysis and up to 3 for the plan; community engagement is scored separately, up to 10 points. Points go to the applicant's analysis of system outcomes and its plan, not to the race of any applicant, owner or tenant. The workbook saved here is the blank template (0 figures filled in).
how: Read from the scoring criteria and the technical-assistance guide; the workbook was opened to see what it asks for.
limits: The files do not give the total points on the whole application or the score any San Francisco project received, so how much these points weighed in an award cannot be said. The award scores would come from the State's Homekey award records for San Francisco projects. The youth department's own equity rules, if any, are not in these files.

rows.rule: Required to apply; scored as complete
3 for a thorough analysis of all disparities in the workbook, 2 for one that addresses all but with superficial examples, 1 if not all are addressed
3 for an actionable, detailed, time-bound plan addressing every barrier, 2 if it lacks detail, 1 if it lacks concrete actions
How the applicant engaged people experiencing or with experience of homelessness, with documentation
